sets.setting: Mixed-density neighborhood near a central business district
sets.design_notes: C and E are close urban-convenience choices with different space and lease compromises; B and F form a close value-versus-quietness comparison. D is an easy budget-and-space trade-off, while A provides a medium balanced comparison.

sets.setting: Outer-suburban rentals for commuters and home-focused renters
sets.design_notes: B and F are close choices: B improves commute and efficiency, while F trades those for light, a very short lease, and nearby essentials. A versus D is a medium cost-space versus access-quality comparison; C and E make easier budget and large-home trade-offs.

sets.setting: Coastal city rentals balancing beach access with city connections
sets.design_notes: A and E are close premium space-and-light choices, separated by rent, lease length, and convenience. C and F are a close modern efficient city option versus a quieter flexible option. B, D, and E establish medium and easy trade-offs around price, size, commute, and outdoor space.

sets.setting: Established inner-ring rentals with varied building types
sets.design_notes: A and C are close compact-city choices with contrasting rent, natural light, and lease flexibility. D and E create a medium size-and-outdoor-space versus cost-and-lease comparison. B and F offer easier low-rent, larger-home choices with distinct commute, noise, and access penalties.
